content:
STAGE 1 - goal: pick a design-space slot not already occupied.
READ: the task brief's list of 17 implemented metrics plus the 'what that means' paragraph.
OBSERVED: every partition-geometry metric fails (hyp_voronoi_margin -0.081, hyp_frechet_cover_radius -0.146, hyp_adj_r2 +0.156, hyp_bucket_reach_lift +0.041). Everything that works uses the frozen Issue #126 reference as a CONTRAST. The current champion HBAA (+0.701) = hyperbolic barycentre of the FULL training history as query point, compared through the reference temperature against the MEAN of ten negative bucket barycentres.
REASONING: the brief names exactly two still-unexploited information sources: (a) the whole training history as the query point, (b) the FULL negative distribution as a temperatured expected rank instead of its mean. HBAA already spends (a), so the only non-redundant slot is (b): keep a history-barycentre query but replace the mean-of-negatives contrast with a soft order statistic over the entire per-cell negative population, then read off the soft rank of the true cell. That is a rank statistic, not a margin, not a likelihood on the path, and not a tightness/coverage number.
ALSO: the brief warns any likelihood-like number must be divided/offset by a size-matched null, because plain path likelihood hit -0.488 by loving collapsed tries; and hbaa_size_matched_kept (+0.061) shows a badly-built null strips the signal. So the null has to be a closed-form chance level, not an estimated one.
OPEN at this point: does a cell-level soft rank of the true cell survive the collapse degeneracy, and is it cheap enough (24587 items, <60 s)?

STAGE 2 - goal: force the null to be exact rather than estimated.
READ: the 'one-code table scores 0 and a randomly relabelled table 0.0003' control in the brief.
OBSERVED/REASONING: with K_eff non-empty level-1 cells, if all cells tie (the zero-information case) a soft rank that uses sigma(beta*(F_true - F_c)) collapses to pi = 1 + (K_eff-1)/2 = (K_eff+1)/2, so 1/pi = 2/(K_eff+1). Therefore subtracting the constant 2/(K_eff+1) is the exact chance level, needs no shuffling, no fitting, and is a function of the codebook alone (contract item 4 satisfied). For K_eff=1 this gives 1-1=0, so a one-code table scores exactly 0, matching the required control. For a random relabel the ties argument holds in expectation, so it scores ~0. This is why I prefer a reciprocal soft rank over a raw likelihood: the chance level is analytic and the collapse case is pinned to 0 rather than rewarded.
OPEN: the size bias of a raw softmin (a 96-item cell always looks closer than a 1-item cell).

STAGE 3 - goal: kill the cell-size bias without a tuned null.
READ: nothing external; this is a derivation.
OBSERVED: rho_c = -(1/beta) log sum_{j in c} exp(-beta d) is monotonically decreasing in |c| for iid draws, so it favours big cells - the same failure that made path likelihood anti-correlate with recall through bucket collapse.
FIX: use the per-item free energy F_c = -(1/beta) log( (1/|c|) sum_{j in c} exp(-beta delta_j) ), i.e. the log-mean-exp of the cell's distance distribution (its log-partition per member). For constant delta this returns delta for every cell regardless of size, so size is neutralised analytically, no shuffling, no second number. This is also a strict generalisation of the mean-of-negatives: it is the soft minimum of the full negative distribution rather than the hard mean, so a single very close negative in the true cell is penalised instead of being averaged away - which is exactly what a 10-candidate Stage-3 re-rank cares about.
OPEN: cost and the leave-one-out bookkeeping for the query barycentre.

STAGE 4 - goal: check the two cheap ways the metric could saturate or leak.
READ: contract items 2 and 3.
OBSERVED/REASONING: (i) the history barycentre m_q is built from the SOURCE representations u_j of the history; if the positive p is left inside, then v_p sits ~0 from m_q in the shared ball and the true cell wins on every pair - the metric would saturate near its ceiling and carry no cross-table signal. So m_q must be the leave-one-out Karcher mean over H_q \ {p}, with the fallback m_q = u_q when the history is a singleton. That uses only TRAINING pairs, so contract 3 holds (no validation, no test, no recall, no Stage-3 artefact).
(ii) curvature: I fix c = -1 exactly as the contract requires 'fixed negative curvature', use the Poincare distance with that c, and take beta = 1/tau_ref from the frozen reference's stored contrastive temperature (its learned inverse temperature/temperature scale if that is what it exposes) - a stored constant of the reference, not a tuned knob.
COST (24587 items, K<=256, d<=64, |T| training pairs): per pair one Karcher mean (|H|*30*d flops, negligible) plus one distance vector over 24587 items (24587*d). Batched as a chunked GEMM (chunk x d) @ (d x 24587) this is ~1.6e10 flops for 1e4 pairs, i.e. ~10-20 s on BLAS at d=64; 5e4 pairs is ~50-60 s. Under a minute. Only level-1 codes are used, so the 12-code/2-code collapses are handled by the K_eff chance level rather than by the geometry.
OPEN: worst-case table.

STAGE 5 - goal: name the table on which the metric must be worst, and confirm it is a legitimate rather than an accidental failure.
OBSERVED/REASONING: the worst case is a HUB-AND-SPOKE level-1 table: each of the K cells holds one geodesically central item (a medoid) plus uniformly random other items. Then every cell's free energy is pinned by its hub, F_c is nearly equal across cells, the sigmoids sit near 1/2, pi -> (K_eff+1)/2 and the metric returns ~0 no matter how good the reference is - the table carries no information about which cell the query's neighbourhood falls in. Second worst: extreme size skew (one giant cell plus 255 singletons) combined with a reference whose distances are dominated by a few hubs; the giant cell wins the soft minimum for every query and true singleton cells accumulate exceedance, driving the metric negative. Both are genuine: the first is a table that is a relabelling of the item list, the second is the collapse direction the brief already flagged. Neither is rewarded, which is the point of subtracting 2/(K_eff+1).
DECISION: proposal fixed. Writing the answer block now.

STAGE 6 - FINAL ANSWER RECORD (condensed; full formula printed in the chat response).
METRIC: hfsc_rank_l1
TITLE: Hyperbolic free-energy cell rank - chance-corrected soft rank of the true level-1 cell under a leave-one-out Karcher barycentre of the full training history, scored against the whole per-cell negative distribution.
FORMULA (core): ball B^d, curvature c=-1; d(x,y)=arcosh(1+2||x-y||^2/((1-||x||^2)(1-||y||^2))). Karcher mean = Riemannian gradient descent, step 1, 30 iters or ||grad||<1e-8, init Euclidean mean projected into the ball. beta=1/tau_ref from the frozen reference's stored contrastive temperature. For each TRAIN pair (q,p): H_q^- = history \ {p}; m_q = KarcherMean({u_j, j in H_q^-}) else u_q; delta_i = d(m_q, v_i) for all i != q. Per cell: F_c = -(1/beta) log( (1/|C_c^-|) sum_{i in C_c^-} e^{-beta delta_i} ) (per-item free energy = size-neutral soft minimum). K_eff = number of non-empty C_c^-. pi_q = 1 + sum_{c != c_p} sigma(beta (F_{c_p}-F_c)); r_q = 1/pi_q. M = mean_TRAIN(r_q) - 2/(K_eff+1).
INPUTS: SID table level-1 code only; frozen Issue #126 reference (u_i, v_i, tau_ref); TRAIN split. Nothing else.
GEOMETRY: curvature enters in d (Poincare Riemannian, diverges at the boundary), in the Karcher mean m_q (the arithmetic mean of the same points is a different ball point), and in the log-partition free energy of the negative population. c=-1 fixed, beta inherited, nothing fitted.
WHY IT TRACKS RECALL: Stage-3 beam reach is capped by whether the true item's level-1 cell is reachable; the metric measures that reachability with the reference. Adds over HBAA/Q_H: (a) HBAA's history barycentre kept, but the mean-of-ten-negatives replaced by a free energy over the entire per-cell negative population, so one near-coincident negative is penalised - which is what the 10-candidate re-rank actually competes against; (b) an order statistic (left tail) instead of a mean; (c) analytic collapse control demanded by the brief.
COMPUTE: one Karcher mean per pair (negligible) + one 24587*d distance vector per pair, chunked GEMM; 1e4 pairs at d=64 ~1.6e10 flops ~10-20 s on BLAS, 5e4 pairs ~50-60 s. K_eff<=256.
RISKS: candidate set narrower than the catalogue; missing tau_ref forces beta=1 (chance offset unaffected); sentinel/empty codes inflate K_eff; singleton-history pairs fall back to u_q; distance saturation ties drive M to 0 (chance), not to a false positive.
FAILURE MODE: worst on a hub-and-spoke table (one geodesic medoid per cell plus random members): all F_c tie, pi -> (K_eff+1)/2, M -> 0. Second worst on extreme size skew (one giant cell + 255 singletons): the giant cell always wins the soft minimum, M goes negative.
END METRIC
